name: PeptideBuilder
summary: Construct short peptide coordinate models from explicitly chosen residue identities and backbone geometry.

argv: import PeptideBuilder as p; from PeptideBuilder import Geometry; g=Geometry.geometry('G'); s=p.initialize_res(g); p.add_residue(s,g); assert sum(1 for _ in s.get_residues())==2; print('PeptideBuilder geometry OK')

notes: This is an MIT-licensed Python library that builds coordinates from user-chosen geometries; it does not predict native peptide folds, rank conformations, dock peptides to proteins or relax a molecular force field. A generated pose requires subsequent scientific review.

The pinned PeptideBuilder distribution is a universal Python wheel; its Biopython dependency still needs a wheel compatible with the host. The installer is wheel-only and will stop rather than compile if a dependency wheel is missing. The package is small (about 14 KB) before Biopython and NumPy dependencies.
Verification creates a two-glycine synthetic model entirely offline and does not write a PDB or process user sequences.
